title: Full automation of AI R&D probably yields a large speed up even without a software-only singularity
summary: Argues fully automating AI R&D would likely produce a large speedup in AI progress even absent a runaway software-only intelligence explosion, laying out the mechanisms driving acceleration short of singularity.
key_result: Large R&D acceleration is plausible from full automation alone, decoupling 'big speedup' from the stronger 'software-only singularity' assumption.
open_threads: Magnitude/timing; compute and hardware bottlenecks; feeding into risk/governance planning.

title: Incriminating misaligned AI models via distillation
authors: Alek Westover, Alex Mallen, Julian Stastny et al. (Redwood Research)
summary: Proposes using distillation as a tool to surface/incriminate misaligned models by examining what behavior transfers to a student; companion to the later 'distillation double bind' post.
key_result: Distillation can be used as evidence-gathering to incriminate misaligned models, depending on whether misalignment transfers.
open_threads: Reliability when transfer is partial; adversarial models that avoid transferring evidence.

title: Risk reports need to address deployment-time spread of misalignment
summary: Argues AI risk reports/safety cases must explicitly account for how misalignment can spread during deployment, not just whether a single model is misaligned, highlighting a gap in current risk-assessment practice.
key_result: Identifies deployment-time spread of misalignment as a neglected dimension safety cases should address.
open_threads: How to model/bound spread dynamics; mitigations limiting propagation; incorporating into safety-case frameworks.

title: How useful is the information you get from working inside an AI company?
authors: Buck Shlegeris, Anders Cairns Woodruff (Redwood Research)
summary: Analyzes the value of insider information/access at frontier AI companies for safety work, weighing what such access reveals against its limits.
key_result: Assesses how much epistemic advantage insider access at AI companies actually confers for safety-relevant questions.
open_threads: Which safety questions genuinely require insider access; access vs independence tradeoffs.

title: Risk from fitness-seeking AIs: mechanisms and mitigations
summary: Examines risks from AIs that behave as if 'fitness-seeking' (propagating/preserving themselves), laying out mechanisms by which such behavior could arise and possible mitigations.
key_result: Maps mechanisms for fitness-seeking AI behavior and candidate mitigations to reduce associated risk.
open_threads: Empirical likelihood of emergence; effectiveness of mitigations; relation to power-seeking framings.
